historical_growth.basis_note: RMB-era only. FY2023-FY2025 are reported in RMB; FY2022 revenue uses the RMB10,900m restated comparative printed in the FY2023 annual report. No RMB restatement exists for FY2022 EPS, equity or FCF, so those 3-year figures are null, and no 5-year figure can be computed without an FX conversion of HKD-era rows that would mix translation effects into operating growth.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: H1 FY2026 revenue run-rate (+4.5% on restated H1 FY2025) with the RMB 2-year revenue CAGR of 7.1% decelerating; GFA grows ~8%/yr but fee rates and contract withdrawals offset part of it
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 2yr CAGR 19.2% vs EPS 2yr CAGR 1.0% and owner-FCF 2yr CAGR -14.7%: book value compounds from a ~42% payout and the Dec-2025 CCPM merger-accounting restatement, not from earnings power. Equity CAGR is NOT used as the growth anchor. Owner FCF fell faster than reported FCF because interest income rose while OCF fell.
historical_growth.notes: FY2023 owner FCF 1,278.8 (1,361.2 - 0.6 SBC - 81.8 interest); FY2024 1,068.6 (1,175.0 + 2.4 - 106.4 - 2.4 reversal treated as nil); FY2025 930.0 (1,033.2 - 0 - 103.2). Three straight years of declining owner FCF on rising revenue: receivables and margin, not volume, are the story.

scenario_narratives.base: Margin reset completes in FY2026 (ex-interest EBITDA ~11.2% vs 12.3% FY2025, 14.4% FY2024), then stabilises at 11% as the mix shifts from residential to urban-space and public-sector contracts; revenue +4% fading to +2.5%; receivables absorb ~25% of incremental revenue; cash at face, NCI at book.
scenario_narratives.bull: Third-party and non-residential wins lift growth to ~6%; procurement and digital efficiency recover margins to 12.5% by year 6; collections normalise as the property cycle troughs; no further elevated related-party transactions.
scenario_narratives.bear: Fee-rate compression and contract withdrawals continue, margins drift to 8.5%, revenue flat for three years, receivables consume a third of any growth, terminal multiple capped at 12x; the cash pile stays trapped behind a ~42% payout and sister-company acquisitions.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A recurring-fee property manager valued on owner free cash flow in RMB with the HKD quote bridged at spot. The valuation is dominated by two things the market is discounting hard: RMB5.7bn of net cash credited at face (about two-thirds of the share price) and a terminal multiple of 12-15x on a cash flow stream whose margin has compressed for two years. The upside the model shows is therefore mostly a judgment that SOE cash will eventually reach shareholders and that margins stabilise rather than halve; the 30% bear weight is where governance and sector-derating risk are charged, not the discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cash credited at face: RMB5.73bn (~HK$2.05/share) sits in PRC subsidiaries and HK; payout ~42% and sister-company acquisitions (CCPM Dec-2025, Project Supervision up to HK$950m announced 2026) mean minority holders may never see it at par

Margin compression not yet proven to have troughed: lump-sum gross margin 14.0% -> 12.4% in FY2025, H1 FY2026 operating profit -10.5%; each 1pp of EBITDA margin is worth roughly RMB0.85/share (~HK$1.0) at the base multiple
Receivables: impairment rate raised to 11.1% in FY2025; H1 FY2026 OCF RMB-502m; the -25% WC capture may be too kind if collections from developers and public bodies keep slipping
Parent linkage: 57% of GFA sourced from the CSCEC/COLI group; a deeper China property downturn shrinks the captive pipeline and the developer-facing value-added segment at the same time
FX: all per-share values are RMB x 1.175; a 5% RMB depreciation against the HKD peg moves every HKD value 5% with no change in the business
Horizon and terminal: ~55-60% of EV is terminal value at a 15x cap; a China PM sector that stays at 6-8x earnings never pays that multiple, so realisation depends on cash return rather than re-rating

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report cash-flow note (Annual_FY2025.txt:8582): share-based payments nil in FY2025, RMB(2.4)m reversal in FY2024, RMB0.6m FY2023. SBC-zero market; equity-award taxes nil.
inputs.buyback_note: Only repurchase on record is RMB11.5m in H1 FY2024 (2.9m shares cancelled). Nothing in FY2025 or H1 FY2026. Flat count is a convention the company does not need to fund because SBC is nil.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (CNY) since the FY2023 annual report; FY2018-FY2022 rows of the Metrics CSV are HKD and are not used in any growth calculation (FY2022 HKD 12,689m vs FY2022 restated RMB 10,900m is a currency change, not a YoY move). Market quote on HKEX is HKD. All per-share values built in RMB then multiplied by CNY/HKD 1.175 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-22T04:18Z). Direction check: USD/CNY ~6.65 and USD/HKD ~7.8 imply ~1.17 HKD per CNY. No dual listing exists for a parity check; dividends are declared in HK cents (FY2025 HK19.0c + HK1.0c special) and paid in HKD at the then rate.
inputs.share_count_basis: 3,283,960,460 shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:2707); basic and diluted EPS are identical in the interim, so no dilutive instruments. Held FLAT: SBC is nil so there is nothing to expense or dilute.
inputs.net_cash_basis: 30 June 2026 interim: cash and cash equivalents RMB3,093.3m plus non-pledged time deposits over three months (RMB2,640.0m) = RMB5,733.3m, matching the CSV cash_and_equivalents row. Restricted bank deposits RMB270.3m excluded (conservative). Bank borrowings nil (RMB111.5m repaid in H1 FY2026). H1 cash is seasonally low: operating cash flow is negative in every first half (receivables collected in H2) and the final dividend is paid mid-year.
inputs.wacc_rationale: RMB-denominated flows, so the rate is built in RMB: 10-year China government bond ~1.8%, China/HK equity risk premium ~6.5-7.0%, beta ~1.1 for an HKEX-listed China property-services name that sold off with its developer parent group. Cost of equity ~9.5%; no debt, so WACC = cost of equity = 9.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios; cyclicality, governance and related-party risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: FY2025 lease principal RMB52.6m (Annual_FY2025.txt:6089) plus lease interest RMB6.2m (line 9376) = RMB58.7m, 0.39% of revenue, charged inside adjusted EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path (0.4%). Lease liabilities (RMB96.1m at 30 June 2026) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt; total_debt is bank borrowings only (nil). D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (~RMB50m of the RMB113.5m FY2025 D&A is ROU), so the lease is charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI deducted once, in the equity bridge at book (RMB76.2m at 30 June 2026, HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:1333). Flows are therefore consolidated: FY2025 profit to NCI was only RMB10.7m (PBT 1,827.9 - tax 450.4 - attributable 1,366.8), so an attributable-only leakage rate would be ~0.8% and is not worth a driver. CCPM (70% owned since Dec-2025, merger-accounted) is the main NCI source.
inputs.ebitda_basis: EBITDA margin path is EX interest income (interest is stripped because the cash pile is added back in the bridge) and AFTER trade-receivable impairment (a real cash cost of this business, not a non-cash add-back). FY2025: operating profit 1,828.1 - interest income 103.2 + D&A 113.5 = 1,838.4 = 12.29% of revenue. FY2024 restated 14.4%, FY2023 13.8%. H1 FY2026 ex-interest EBIT margin 11.8% vs 13.6% in H1 FY2025, and H2 margins run ~3-4pp below H1 in this company, so FY2026E ~11.2%.
inputs.tax_basis: Cash tax rate applied to EBIT after D&A and lease charge. Book tax FY2025 RMB450.4m on PBT 1,827.9 (24.6%); cash taxes paid 523.2 (FY2025) and 453.0 (FY2024) against ex-interest EBIT of 1,724.9 and 1,912.6 average ~27%. Statutory PRC 25% plus 5-10% withholding on dividends repatriated from PRC subsidiaries explains the premium. Calibration: FY0 NOPAT at 27% on ex-interest, post-lease EBIT (1,666) is RMB1,216m vs attributable net income ex after-tax interest income of ~RMB1,289m; the gap is lease interest and cash-vs-book timing.
inputs.working_capital_basis: Receivables build consumes cash as the book grows: FY2025 OCF ex interest received and gross of tax paid (1,153.5 - 62.0 + 523.2 = 1,614.7) was RMB224m below ex-interest EBITDA (1,838.4), i.e. -24% of the RMB936m revenue increase; FY2024 -329m / -34%; FY2023 roughly nil. Trade receivable impairment rate was raised to 11.1% in FY2025 and H1 FY2026 OCF was RMB-501.6m vs -71.4m restated. wc_capture_pct is therefore NEGATIVE: -25% base, -15% bull (collections normalise), -35% bear.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (owner_fcf_dcf_component) via .claude/skills/dcf-methods SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US', with the adaptations file applied (dual currency RMB/HKD, leases treatment B, NCI in bridge, SBC-zero, risk charged once). Fresh build, no prior DCF or memory entry. COPL is a fee-for-service property manager with recurring lump-sum management fees (77% of revenue), not a REIT, developer or holdco; its cash flows are the valuation object. SBC-ZERO MARKET: house and street bases coincide, band_position is null. CASH AT FACE: RMB5.73bn net cash is ~HK$2.05/share, ~64% of the market price, credited at face value in the bridge; the market applies a discount for SOE cash retention (payout ~42%) and related-party M&A (FY2025 CCPM subscription from CSCEC; announced acquisition of Project Supervision Ltd from CSCI/CSCD affiliates for up to HK$950m, which Nomura called elevated and which knocked the shares ~15%). That deal is NOT deducted from cash because it buys an earnings stream absent from the flows; if it closes at HK$950m and is worth, say, 70% of that, the value leakage is ~HK$0.09/share. HORIZON: 10 years so that the margin reset (FY2026 compression then stabilisation) is complete before capitalising. Year-1 owner FCF from the components is ~RMB960m vs FY2025 owner FCF RMB930m; H1 FY2026 cash generation says FY2026 could print below that, which the -25% WC capture only partly reflects. Half-year rows (H1 FY2024/25/26) carry negative OCF by seasonality and were not used as FCF anchors. FY2018-FY2022 HKD rows excluded from every CAGR.

bear.narrative: The lump-sum margin slide (14.0% to 12.4% in FY2025) continues as price competition and contract withdrawals persist, value-added services to non-residents stay loss-making, and developer-facing engineering/pre-delivery work shrinks with COLI's pipeline. Revenue stalls for three years, receivables impairment keeps rising (11.1% rate and climbing), and the terminal multiple is capped at 12x to reflect a sector that no longer re-rates. Related-party cash deployment is the unmodelled tail: cash credited at face here is the first thing a bear would haircut.

base.narrative: FY2026 completes the margin reset seen in H1 (ex-interest EBITDA 11.2%), then margins hold at 11% as low-margin residential withdrawals are replaced by urban-space and public-sector contracts at similar economics. Revenue grows 4% fading to 2.5% as GFA growth (~8%) is offset by fee pressure. Receivables keep absorbing a quarter of incremental revenue. Terminal value is Gordon-bound at 14.6x year-10 FCF (9.5% WACC, 2.5% growth), just under the 15x cap, so the cap and Gordon give almost the same answer.

bull.narrative: Urban-space operator pivot and third-party wins (85.9% of new GFA) lift growth to 6% near term; procurement platform and Xinghai Wulian digitalisation recover margins to the FY2025 level of 12.5% by year 6; receivables normalise as the property downturn troughs; CCPM and Project Supervision integrate without further elevated related-party deals.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% from the 15% default: attributable profit has fallen for three consecutive reporting periods on rising revenue, H1 FY2026 operating cash flow was RMB-502m against -71m a year earlier, the lump-sum gross margin trend is unbroken, and the pending HK$950m related-party Project Supervision purchase shows the cash pile is deployed at the parent group's discretion. Bull cut to 20% because it needs margin recovery AND receivables normalisation AND related-party discipline to all hold at once. Base 50%: the recurring fee base, SOE tenders and Hong Kong franchise make outright decline unlikely.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
